AMZN.rationale: Amazon is a structurally durable franchise with multiple self-reinforcing growth engines (AWS at 32% cloud share with $244B backlog, $85B advertising run rate, dominant e-commerce). Revenue grew +13.4% YoY and EPS +36.4% YoY in Q3 2025, with robust OCF growth of +36.8% YoY and a fortress balance sheet (D/E 0.149). However, the stock has re-rated from 29x to 36x PE in two months on pure multiple expansion with no earnings acceleration — net margin and ROE are identical at both points. Operating income was flat YoY in Q3 despite 13.4% revenue growth, suggesting margin pressure beneath the surface. WTI crude at $99.27 (+64% in 90 days) is a material cost headwind for a logistics-intensive business, and the 3.5% fuel surcharge on 3P sellers signals management sees this pressure. The $200B capex commitment for 2026 has compressed FCF to $11.2B from $38.2B. At 36x PE near the 365-day high of $258.79, the stock is priced at the upper end of its range and demands continued elevated execution. The Q1 2026 earnings report on April 29 is a credible near-term catalyst — BofA models AWS growth of 28% and EBIT of $21.4B above consensus — but this is a verification event rather than a clear re-rating catalyst, and the stock has already rallied ~30% in recent weeks. The franchise quality supports a premium, but valuation already embeds much of the upside, warranting a mildly positive but not strongly bullish score.
